decisions.rationale: BHSA sp.md line 17 defines art as article. No reviewed Article class is pinned in the current OLiA lock; native-only is a provisional proposal, not proof that there is no ontology equivalent.
BHSA sp.md line 22 defines prep as preposition. A reviewed Preposition target is not pinned by the current ontology lock; native-only is proposed pending external class-level evidence.
BHSA sp.md line 23 defines conj as conjunction. The current lock has no independently reviewed Conjunction class target; native-only is proposed conservatively, not as an absolute absence claim.
BHSA sp.md line 24 defines prps as personal pronoun. Its subtype cannot simply be equated with the general Syriac pron category; native-only is proposed without a reviewed target.
BHSA sp.md line 25 defines prde as demonstrative pronoun. It is not silently equivalent to general pronoun or interrogative pronoun; native-only is proposed pending specific target evidence.
BHSA sp.md line 26 defines prin as interrogative pronoun, distinct from inrg interrogative particle. No corresponding reviewed shared-target class is pinned, so native-only is proposed.
BHSA sp.md line 27 defines intj as interjection. The present pinned OLiA subset does not contain a reviewed Interjection target; this is a conservative native-only proposal pending evidence.
BHSA sp.md line 28 defines nega as negative particle. It cannot be equated to general negation or an unverified OLiA class; native-only is proposed while a precise target is unreviewed.
BHSA sp.md line 29 defines inrg as interrogative particle, not the interrogative pronoun prin. No reviewed equivalent target is pinned, so native-only is a scoped provisional candidate.
The ETCBC linksyr grammar line 91 defines Syriac sp=pron as pronoun; it does not specify BHSA prps/prde/prin subtypes. Without pinned target-level evidence, native-only is proposed provisionally.
